text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The industry ministry will ask the government to endorse plans to cut the price for natural gas.
- The ruling coalition is expected to designate candidates for the jobs of chairmen at the state-run banks.
- The purchasing price for wheat rose 30 percent to 1,036 lei per kilogram.
- The government will submit parliament for approval a new law for the mining sector.
- Checks carried out by customs authorities at Romania's border are lax, the paper says.
- The process started last week by commercial banks to give credits to the farming sector proceeds at slow pace.
- Floods affected five counties across Romania.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Parliament will start talks on the new budget next week.
- The ~Avicola Codlea~state-run poultry farm cut 300 jobs.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The industry ministry started to restructure the mining sector.
- The Bucharest city-hall needs some $500 million to ensure sufficient fresh water supplies and repair the pipelines.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Some 700,000 law suits were registered in Romania following the implementation of a 1991 land restitution law.
- Max Van der Stoel, the OSCE's High Commissioner for minority and human rights, hailed the Romanian government for the way it handles issues related to ethnic minorities.
ADEVARUL
- The government drafted a law to cut taxes on advertising and publicity. The law would not apply to cigarettes and beverages traders.
- Farmers in the Covasna county plan to donate 30,000 tonnes of potatoes to North Korea.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The opposition Party of Social Democracy and the Socialist Labour Party will sign a political accord to create the "leftist front".

- Some 80 percent of Romanians want their country to join NATO in an early stage, a poll showed. The majority of those polled said failure to join the Western alliance would bring a period of instability for the country and would enhance Russia's influence in the region.
- Romanian-born businessman and agent Marcel Avram, major shareholder in the local Tele7 ABC private television, was arrested in Germany for tax evasion worth 8.0 million marks.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania and Hungary must join NATO at the same time, Max Van der Stoel told Romanian presidential adviser Zoe Petre.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
